court_name: Superior Court of California, County of Stanislaus
case_search_note: The court's 'Search for a Case' page links to the Public, Justice Partner, and Attorney Portal, which it says lets you search public case information and make traffic payments. The page does not say whether criminal cases are included. In person, the Criminal Division has a court-provided computer, or you can submit a Research Request Form; a $15 research fee may apply if you don't know your case number (Criminal FAQs). Criminal Division: (209) 530-3100 option 4, Criminal.Requests@stanct.org.

courthouses.name: Main Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Mon–Fri 8:15 a.m.–4:00 p.m. (Criminal Division phone line Mon–Fri 8:15 a.m.–3:00 p.m.)
courthouses.note: Main criminal courthouse. Criminal Clerk's Office is 1st floor, Room 140 (11th St entrance); Self-Help Center 2nd floor, Room 220. Mailing: P.O. Box 1098, Modesto, CA 95353. Criminal email: Criminal.Requests@stanct.org; Zoom link requests (pre-authorized counsel/pro per only): criminalzoomrequests@stanct.org. Per the Sheriff's Court Services page, courtrooms here handle arraignments, preliminary hearings, and misdemeanor and felony trials. Department list from the court's Judicial Assignments page effective 9/1/2026 — assignments rotate.

legal_aid.name: Stanislaus County Public Defender — Clean Slate Program
legal_aid.serves: People with Stanislaus County convictions only
legal_aid.what: Post-conviction relief. Apply with the online Clean Slate Form; you must not be serving a sentence, on probation/parole/PRCS, or facing a pending charge. Not everyone qualifies and it may take a few months. Do not submit duplicate applications.

legal_aid.name: California Rural Legal Assistance (CRLA) — Modesto Headquarters
legal_aid.serves: Low-income residents of rural California; Modesto office
legal_aid.what: Lists Criminal Record Clearing among its legal help areas. CRLA has held free Clean Slate clinics in Modesto with the Stanislaus DA, Public Defender and Probation (most recent found: Nov 7, 2025).
legal_aid.todo: No upcoming 2026 Stanislaus clinic date found; office hours not listed

legal_aid.name: Stanislaus Superior Court Self-Help Center
legal_aid.what: Free help with court forms and procedures; its service list includes expungements. Walk-ins first-come, first-served. Staff cannot give legal advice.

programs.name: Probation Pretrial Services Unit
programs.summary: Probation officers complete pretrial assessments on adults booked into custody on new charges and give the results to judges, who decide on release or detention. People released are monitored, must report to Probation and sign a pretrial monitoring agreement, and get court-date reminders.
programs.todo: No dedicated pretrial phone number published; Adult Division number shown

programs.name: Day Reporting Center (DRC)
programs.summary: Probation-run center (with the Sheriff and BHRS) for people released from custody: assessment with a validated risk tool plus programs including high school equivalency prep, tattoo removal, job search/placement, vocational training, batterer's and child abuse treatment, substance use disorder treatment and cognitive behavioral classes.

programs.summary: The Sheriff's Jail Alternatives Unit runs a Home Detention Program and an Alternative Work Program that may let eligible people serve a sentence while keeping regular employment.

programs.name: Court Self-Help Center
programs.summary: 800 11th Street, Room 220, Modesto. Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. and 1:00–4:00 p.m.; walk-ins first-come, first-served. Voicemail (209) 548-6237 (calls returned Wednesdays); email Self.Help@StanCt.org. Services include expungements.

jails.name: Sheriff's Detention Center – East (SDC-East)
jails.phone_note: Booking and releasing facility (opened 2017); up to 559 people; includes maximum-security, mental health and hospital units. Video visits only (JailATM.com account); no visiting Wednesdays; two free 30-minute video visits per week.
jails.court_ids_note: The Sheriff's Court Services page says it transports all inmates to court; arraignments, preliminary hearings and misdemeanor/felony trials are at the Main Courthouse (800 11th St). Specific court assignment depends on the case. The Sheriff also runs one court holding facility (not listed separately).
jails.todo: Sheriff's page does not say whether men, women or both are housed here (it is the booking facility for all arrestees).

bail.note: Before paying a bail agent, check that their license is active with the California Department of Insurance license lookup. The court's bail schedules are linked from the Criminal Division page (https://www.stanislaus.courts.ca.gov/divisions/criminal/bail-schedules). To find someone in custody, use the Sheriff's 'Who's in Jail' search (name, DOB or 7-digit booking number). This is information only, not legal advice.
